name: Society Pass Incorporated

profile.description: Society Pass was a Southeast Asia-focused digital ecosystem company operating across Singapore, Vietnam, Indonesia, the Philippines, and Thailand in digital marketing, lifestyle, beauty, travel, and food & beverage verticals. Under CEO Raynauld Liang (replacing founder Dennis Nguyen), the company announced a December 2025 pivot to AI-driven data centre and telecoms investments. On May 12, 2026, Society Pass and its SoPa subsidiary filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in Houston (Case No. 26-90525), and Nasdaq moved to delist shares on May 21, 2026. The stock is delisted and effectively untradeable. The most recently reported quarter showed revenue of ~$2.05M with TTM revenue of ~$7.1M and TTM net losses of ~$10.2M.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (0/3): Society Pass failed to establish a viable business model in five years of operation. Revenue peaked at approximately $7.2M annually while losing $10.2M, the company filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy in May 2026, and Nasdaq initiated delisting proceedings [1][2]. The multi-vertical digital platform strategy across five Southeast Asian countries spread resources too thin without achieving scale in any category. The December 2025 announced pivot to 'AI-driven data centre and telecoms' was a desperate strategy shift with no execution before bankruptcy [4]. AI Deployment (0/2): No evidence of AI product deployment, AI-driven cost savings, or meaningful AI strategy. The December 2025 announcement of AI data centre investments was pure aspiration with zero execution before the May 2026 bankruptcy filing [4]. Market Share (0/2): Society Pass was a micro-cap participant with negligible market share in the Southeast Asian digital economy, competing against well-funded platforms like Grab, Shopee, and GoTo with orders-of-magnitude more capital and users. The 3.3M registered users and 205K merchants are trivial by regional standards. Product Pipeline (0/2): No viable product pipeline. The company entered Chapter 11 bankruptcy and its operational focus shifted to survival and restructuring rather than product development [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No evidence of meaningful R&D spending. TTM revenue of $7.1M and losses of $10.2M leave no resources for research and development.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): Society Pass's stated purpose as a digital ecosystem connecting consumers and merchants across Southeast Asia is generic — interchangeable with dozens of e-commerce platforms in the region. No distinctive vision or deeper purpose beyond building a marketplace was identified. The mission does not articulate why Society Pass exists beyond commercial opportunity. Community Impact (0/2): No evidence of charitable giving, community programs, or social impact initiatives. A company with $7.1M in TTM revenue, net losses of $10.2M, and bankruptcy proceedings had no resources for community investment [1]. Employee Retention (0/2): No employee retention data available. The Chapter 11 filing and Nasdaq delisting suggest severe organizational instability that would drive employee departures [1]. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of insider buying. The stock's collapse and bankruptcy filing make open-market purchases inconceivable.

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: LIQUIDITY FLOOR TRIGGERED: The stock was delisted from Nasdaq on May 21, 2026, following the Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing. yfinance returns no data — stock price, volume, and all financial metrics are unavailable, indicating the stock is effectively untradeable [3]. Infrastructure score is automatically set to 0. Even before delisting, the stock traded at approximately $0.37 with average daily volume of ~331,000 shares, yielding daily dollar volume of approximately $122,000 — well below the $1,000,000 minimum. Underlying financial metrics were uniformly dire: ROE deeply negative (TTM losses of $10.2M on $7.1M revenue = -143% profit margin), revenue declining, and the company in bankruptcy proceedings with assets subject to creditor claims [1][2].

ai_resilience.label: HIGH RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (4/9): Society Pass operated a digital marketing and e-commerce platform — a sector with meaningful AI exposure. AI-powered marketing tools (automated ad creative, personalized targeting, content generation) are rapidly displacing the manual digital marketing services that small platforms provide [2]. AI-native e-commerce platforms from major players (Shopee's AI recommendations, Grab's AI-driven services) widen the competitive gap in Southeast Asia. However, local merchant relationships and physical-world commerce connections provide some protection from purely digital AI disruption. The company's existential threat was not AI but financial insolvency — in a hypothetical recovery scenario, AI disruption would be a material risk to the business model. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI revenue. The December 2025 announcement of AI data centre investments was aspirational with zero execution before the May 2026 bankruptcy [4].

infinite_game.summary: Society Pass is the definition of a finite-game failure. A company in Chapter 11 bankruptcy with Nasdaq delisting is not playing an infinite game — it is fighting for its right to continue existing. The company expanded into 5 countries across multiple verticals without achieving product-market fit in any of them, a pattern of growth-at-all-costs thinking that prioritizes expansion metrics over sustainable value creation [1]. The December 2025 strategy pivot to AI data centres — announced five months before bankruptcy — reveals a company chasing trends rather than building on a durable foundation.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (0/3): No Just Cause is evident. Society Pass existed to build a digital marketplace in Southeast Asia, which is a commercial objective, not a vision of a future state that inspires sacrifice. The company's multi-country, multi-vertical strategy followed by a last-minute pivot to AI data centres suggests opportunistic trend-chasing rather than purpose-driven decision-making. The Chapter 11 filing is the ultimate evidence that the company optimized for expansion over sustainability [1].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Chapter 11 bankruptcy and Nasdaq delisting destroy organizational trust. Employees face immediate job insecurity, creditors are enforcing claims, and the company's future is uncertain [1]. The CEO transition from founder Dennis Nguyen to Raynauld Liang suggests leadership instability. Operations across 5 countries with ~200 employees indicate a thinly-spread organization with limited capacity for building organizational depth or trust.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No evidence of competitive self-awareness or rival acknowledgment. Society Pass operated in markets dominated by Grab, Shopee, GoTo, and established local players with vastly superior resources, but there is no evidence the company learned from these rivals' strengths or used competitive pressure to improve its own offerings. The multi-vertical expansion appears to have ignored rather than learned from competitors' focused strategies.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (0/2): Society Pass did not demonstrate strategic flexibility. The company maintained its multi-country, multi-vertical platform strategy even as revenue declined and losses mounted, suggesting rigidity rather than adaptation [2]. The December 2025 pivot to AI data centres was announced but never executed, and the May 2026 Chapter 11 filing rendered it moot [4]. A forced restructuring driven by financial distress is not the kind of existential flexibility Sinek describes.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): No evidence of courageous leadership decisions. The company expanded aggressively across 5 countries while burning cash at a rate far exceeding revenue, ultimately ending in bankruptcy — this represents reckless capital allocation rather than the kind of courage Sinek describes [1]. No examples of leadership sacrificing short-term results for long-term capability, investing during downturns, or taking principled stances.

investment_thesis: There is no bull case for Society Pass. The company filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy on May 12, 2026, Nasdaq suspended trading on May 21, 2026, and the stock is effectively untradeable [1]. TTM revenue of $7.1M against net losses of $10.2M demonstrates a business model that fundamentally does not work — the company burned $1.43 for every $1 in revenue generated [2]. The last-minute December 2025 pivot to AI data centre investments was never executed and served only to highlight the company's strategic desperation. Even the Inspire Impact Score of 33 (ALIGNED) cannot offset the complete destruction of shareholder value.
thesis_continued: The risks are existential and immediate. Chapter 11 restructuring may not result in a viable going concern — the company's assets (registered users and merchant relationships across 5 Southeast Asian countries) have highly uncertain value in bankruptcy proceedings, and creditor enforcement has been stayed but not eliminated [1]. Nasdaq delisting eliminates institutional investor access and liquidity. Even if the company emerges from bankruptcy, the competitive landscape in Southeast Asian digital commerce is dominated by Grab, Shopee, and GoTo, all of which have orders-of-magnitude more capital, technology, and market share. The Q2 2025 positive EPS of $0.10 appears to have been a one-off outlier in a consistently loss-making business, and the ~$15M cash balance reported earlier is now subject to bankruptcy proceedings and legal/restructuring costs [2][3].
key_catalysts: Successful Chapter 11 restructuring and emergence as a viable going concern — though this is highly speculative and depends on court approval, creditor agreement, and operational turnaround that has never been demonstrated [1]
Potential strategic acquisition of the company's user base (3.3M registered users) and merchant network (205K) by a larger Southeast Asian digital platform at a premium to distressed value
Nasdaq delisting appeal success and restoration of trading — though this appears unlikely given the bankruptcy filing and multiple prior compliance violations [1][3]
key_risks: Chapter 11 bankruptcy may result in complete equity wipeout — shareholders are last in line behind secured creditors, unsecured creditors, and preferred holders in any liquidation scenario [1]
Stock is delisted and untradeable, eliminating any ability for investors to exit positions or for new capital to enter, creating a permanent capital trap for remaining shareholders [3]

Revenue declining 18% YoY while operating at a -143% profit margin demonstrates a fundamentally broken business model with no clear path to profitability even under optimistic restructuring scenarios [2]
